problem: Pull requests are slow to write, review and merge; Squire drafted PR descriptions, reviewed PRs and implemented review feedback.
product_category: AI code review / pull request assistant

founders.name: Karl Clement
previous_startups: Codex, VS Code extension (co-founder; outcome not checked)
founders.background_notes: YC page: fullstack engineer, building companies since 14.

technical_complexity.rationale: Code-understanding with LLMs in 2021 (GPT-3 era) was workable but unreliable; integration with GitHub is routine.

defensibility.rationale: No proprietary data or lock-in is described; the wedge could be reproduced by any code-hosting platform or LLM vendor.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GitHub Copilot launched as a technical preview in mid-2021 and later added PR features; I did not find a dated source tying this to Squire, so this is context, not a sourced cause.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand for AI pull-request assistance in 2021 was found in the sources checked; the YC page only describes the product.

branding.domain_note: squire.ai now shows a registrar expired-domain page (checked this session).

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly tagline on the YC page but no press, community or merch evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Squire.ai was an eight-person YC S21 AI pull-request assistant that the directory lists as Inactive and whose domain has lapsed. No shutdown post, founder post-mortem, funding record or acquisition was found, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Extruct reports US$60M raised on 2021-07-28 (Tiger Global, ICONIQ) and US$10-15M revenue; implausible for an 8-person company and contradicted by Bounce Watch (no funding data); treated as erroneous and not recorded. A 'commoditized AI' blog blames Copilot; opinion piece, not used. Shutdown date unknown. Web Archive skipped.
